page.layout: One page of text in a single column. Margin notes on the right, beside the first lines of the column. Running head at top, page number at top right. Signature and catchword at the foot.

main_text.p: Si voluntas est absoluta, tum Deus decreto absoluto determinavit omnes liberas conversiones omnium electorum, & per eandem rationem omnes etiam liberas non-conversiones reproborum. Ferrum prius quam hoc decoxerit Itomachus[?] Jesuiticus aut. Arminianus. O jam tollitur (inquiunt) libertas, evertitur omnis religio, introducitur fatum, Stoicismus, Manechismus, & quid non? Suis hic opitulari cupit Grevinchov. ita etiam & nobile ingenium Petri Fonsecae. Tit. 216[?]. Omnia volunt reduci ad decretum absolutum, ut in causam altissimam. 217. Ita enim illi, si Petrus in hisce & non in aliis occasionibus & rerum ordine collocabitur, & tali modo dispositus vocabitur, tum obsequetur divinae vocationi. Sed ego decerno (inquit Deus) absolute collocare Petrum in tali rerum ordine, & ipsum tali modo dispositum vocare. Ergo absoluta mea voluntas prima est causa, cur Petrus meae obsequatur vocationi. Sed Resp. 2. Non est hic primus & altissimus ille syllogismus in quem reducetur tota vocationis efficacia, 1. Major non est necessaria, imo stante indifferentia Jesuitica & Arminiana in voluntate Petri, non magis vera quam falsa, & falsa, quam vera est major propositio connexa. Nam in quocunque rerum ordine collocetur Petrus, nunquid ille ordo ipsius voluntatem ad assentiendem Dei vocationi determinabit? Num quaefo tantum convivium, mens hilaris, timor aliquis gehennae aut ejusmodi

page.notes: Tit. 216 is hard to read in the margin; the number after it may be 216 or 2i6. The running head and page number are set in spaced small capitals and are partly unclear. "Itomachus" is uncertain. The word "Stoicismus" was read from a long-s form. The final line ends the page and runs into the catchword "modi". Shows some show-through from the opposite side, which was not transcribed.
